newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso rallies in range-trading.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso rallies in range-trading.

text.p: The Philippine peso bounced back on Tuesday to close at 26.277 from 26.280 in range-trading, traders said.
Banks continued to sell their dollars in order to assuage their peso liquidity positions, traders said.
But "some banks tried to stir up the market by bidding up the dollar. They wanted to create opportunities for trading profits," said dealer from a big bank.
Some banks used as an excuse the $30 million requirement of oil companies on Wednesday to weaken the peso, dealers said.
That resulted in a lower peso average of 26.276 to the dollar versus the previous day's 26.272.
Dealers said the Central Bank initially raised its desired trading range for the peso at a bid and offer rate of 26.23 and 26.28 to the dollar compared with the prior 26.235 and 26.285.
It later brought its rates to former levels after some foreign banks bought up the dollar, traders said.
